newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Bonos closed almost unchanged on Monday, only a little higher than at Friday's end, after a very nervous day with little trade but sharp movements in prices.
"At the end, after big expectations we didn't see anything," a dealer in Madrid said. With very little domestic news Spain's bond market was focusing on the Italian Btps, dealers said.

Early on, the market didn't know how to react to the lira re-entry to the ERM, later it fell on news that an Italian prosecutor was recommending that Prime Minister Romano Prodi be tried for alleged abuse of office during his chairmanship of state holding company IRI. It ended little changed.
"I do not think tomorrow is going to be different," a dealer said. "With Thanksgiving in the States this week it's going to be a very quiet one," another said.
The 10-year spread with Germany, which dipped earlier to an all-time record low of 128 basis points, was trading near the close at 131 bp, unchanged from Friday.

Dealers said the Bank of Spain was selling pesetas versus the mark at levels between 84.09 and 84.11. The central bank declined to comment, as usual. The peseta was trading almost unchanged at 84.09/12 to the mark at the end of the day.
